summary: Karin Preisendanz works in Indology and philosophy. She held posts at the University of Hamburg from around 1989 to 1996 and served as Professor at the University of Vienna from around 1999 to 2023.

Karl Brugmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius from around 1868 to 1871. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1884–1887) and Leipzig University (~1887–1919).

Karl Brunnhölzl works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung and teacher Jenny Purtle, later serving as curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University in 1880. He later served there from around 1893 to 1925 as University Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages.

Karl Florenz specialized in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. He held posts as professor at the University of Tokyo from around 1889 to 1914 and at the University of Hamburg from around 1914 to 1934.

Karl Friedrich Geldner studied Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and at Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Marburg.

Karl H. Potter was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Harvard University in 1955. He was a professor at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1971) and later held a post at the University of Washington (attested 1987–1999).

Karl Hoffmann was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Saarland University from around 1952 to 1955 and as professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from around 1955 to 1983.

Karl Jettmar worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from around 1958 to 1964 and at Heidelberg University from around 1964 to 1986.

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1824–1826), Heidelberg University (~1826–1827), and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1827–1828). He held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1828 to 1833.
Karl Verner was a linguist who studied at Aarhus Katedralskole. He held a post at the University of Copenhagen from around 1883 to 1896.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1980). He held posts at the Ifo Institute, LMU Munich, and as professor at both Würzburg-Schweinfurt and the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo completed a doctorate in comparative philosophy at the University of Hawaii. She held posts at Chaminade University, East-West Center, Jamyang Foundation, University of San Diego, and the University of California, San Diego (attested 2013).

Karma Phuntsho completed his PhD at Oxford (Balliol College) under Michael Aris and David Seyfort Ruegg, having earlier attended Yangchenphug Higher Secondary School. He held a post-doctoral position at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique from around 2003 to 2005.

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies before earning a PhD at the University of Tasmania under doctoral supervisors Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Ura studied at Magdalen College, Oxford (~1983–1986) and the University of Edinburgh (~1988–1989). Working in Tibetology and other fields, he became Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies around 1999.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. In 1991, he is attested as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal studied at the University of Allahabad and the University of Oxford (Jesus College) from around 1906 to 1909. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta in 1917.
